prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The map separates a near left wall/door plane from the darker, more distant room and shows one person centered in frames 2–5, roughly 1.5–2.5 m from the camera wearer; the person appears nearer in frame 3, farther in frame 4, then nearer again in frame 5. In frame 3, the person is in front of a couch about 1–2 m behind them, while pale cushions or nearby furniture sit to their left and a tall dark object is to their right; the person partly occludes these objects. In frames 4–5, the person shifts from center-left to right and remains oriented generally toward the camera, while the background stays several metres farther away. Depth makes foreground/background separation and relative distance changes clearer than RGB, but the estimates are approximate and unreliable along frame seams, reflective glass, object boundaries, and the partly visible person at the far-left edge of frame 1.
descriptions.segmentation: The map consistently isolates one main person in frames 2–5, located near center in frame 2, center-right in frame 3, center-left in frame 4, and right in frame 5; the masks indicate substantial overlap with the background but do not encode metric distance. In frame 3 it additionally marks a couch behind and to the person’s right, a narrow object labeled “surfboard” to the left of that couch, and a rectangular object labeled “refrigerator” above/behind it, although the RGB context makes the last two labels doubtful. The person faces approximately toward the camera in frames 2, 4, and 5 and is more obliquely oriented in frame 3; no other fully segmented person is shown, despite a partly visible figure at the far-left edge of frame 1. Segmentation clarifies object silhouettes and occlusion—especially the person blocking furniture—but provides no direct range or arm’s-reach information, misses most walls and furnishings, and appears unreliable for the unusual object classes in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map places a partially visible body segment at the extreme left in frame 1, a distant upper-body/face trace near center in frame 2, a much larger full upper-body skeleton near center-right in frame 3, a smaller sparse face-and-shoulder trace near center-left in frame 4, and a face/shoulder trace on the right in frame 5. This scale change supports the person being closest in frame 3—approximately 1–2 m away and potentially near the outer limit of arm’s reach—and farther away in frames 2, 4, and 5, roughly 2–3 m; their detected face remains broadly directed toward the camera. In frame 3, one magenta hand is low and to the person’s right while the other arm extends downward on the left side of their body; in frame 5, a magenta hand cluster appears above the detected face/shoulder region, though its placement is uncertain. Pose reveals limb orientation, body scale, and partial-body truncation more clearly than RGB, but many joints are missing or misplaced, the frame-5 hand detection looks especially unreliable, and the sparse traces cannot establish precise distances or whether contact is possible.
